name: x25_connect
prose: Connects an X.25 socket. It takes lock_sock(sk) on entry and every return goes through the single release_sock(sk) at label out. Return paths in order: (1) sk_state is TCP_ESTABLISHED and sock->state is SS_CONNECTING: sets sock->state to SS_CONNECTED and returns 0 (a connect that completed during an interrupted wait), no route or neighbour is taken. (2) sk_state is TCP_CLOSE and sock->state is SS_CONNECTING: sets sock->state to SS_UNCONNECTED and returns -ECONNREFUSED. (3) -EISCONN if sk_state is TCP_ESTABLISHED. (4) -EALREADY if sk_state is TCP_SYN_SENT. Paths 3 and 4 change nothing. Otherwise sk_state is set to TCP_CLOSE and sock->state to SS_UNCONNECTED and then: (5) -EINVAL if addr_len is not sizeof(struct sockaddr_x25), the family is not AF_X25, or x25_addr has no NUL within X25_ADDR_LEN bytes (no references taken). (6) -ENETUNREACH if x25_get_route finds no route (no references taken). (7) -ENETUNREACH if x25_get_neigh returns NULL for the route device: the route reference is released (out_put_route), x25->neighbour is not touched. (8) -ENETUNREACH if x25_new_lci returns 0 (rc still holds the value set before the route lookup), and (9) -EINVAL if SOCK_ZAPPED is set (socket not bound); on paths 8 and 9 the neighbour reference is released, x25->neighbour is set to NULL, x25->state is set to X25_STATE_0 and the route reference is released. Otherwise the destination address is stored, sock->state becomes SS_CONNECTING, sk_state TCP_SYN_SENT, x25->state X25_STATE_1, a Call Request is written and the heartbeat and T21 timers are started. Then: (10) -EINPROGRESS if sk_state is not TCP_ESTABLISHED and O_NONBLOCK is set: this jumps to out, so the neighbour reference stays in x25->neighbour and the route reference taken by x25_get_route is NOT released on this path. (11) Otherwise it calls x25_wait_for_connection_establishment; a nonzero result (for example -ERESTARTSYS, a pending socket error or -ENOTCONN) is returned after the neighbour reference is released (x25->neighbour NULL, x25->state X25_STATE_0) and the route reference is released. (12) On a zero result sock->state becomes SS_CONNECTED and 0 is returned, keeping the neighbour reference in x25->neighbour and releasing the route reference.
note: slice cut the head; real function x25_connect at af_x25.c:746. Reviewer right on both points: the -EINPROGRESS path (af_x25.c 'goto out' after rc = -EINPROGRESS) skips x25_route_put, and the no-LCI path (goto out_put_neigh with rc still -ENETUNREACH) returns -ENETUNREACH not -EINVAL. Old prose was also wrong that the route ref is released on -EINPROGRESS.

name: x25_state1_machine
prose: Handles one received frame for a socket in X25_STATE_1 (awaiting Call Accepted). Both return statements in the function return 0, and the function itself never frees skb. Switch on frametype. X25_CALL_ACCEPTED: stops the timer, resets condition, vs, va, vr and vl to 0, sets x25->state to X25_STATE_3 and sk->sk_state to TCP_ESTABLISHED, then parses the frame: if pskb_may_pull(skb, X25_STD_MIN_LEN) fails, if x25_parse_address_block or x25_parse_facilities returns a negative value, or if the remaining data is longer than X25_MAX_CUD_LEN, it goes to out_clear; otherwise it pulls the header, address block and facilities, copies any remaining Call User Data (when skb->len > 0) into x25->calluserdata and, if SOCK_DEAD is not set, calls sk_state_change. X25_CALL_REQUEST (call collision): sets causediag cause 0x01 and diagnostic 0x48, writes a Clear Request and calls x25_disconnect(sk, EISCONN, 0x01, 0x48). X25_CLEAR_REQUEST: if pskb_may_pull(skb, X25_STD_MIN_LEN + 2) fails it goes to out_clear; otherwise it writes a Clear Confirmation and calls x25_disconnect(sk, ECONNREFUSED, skb->data[3], skb->data[4]). Any other frametype does nothing. out_clear writes a Clear Request, sets x25->state to X25_STATE_2 and starts the T23 timer, without calling x25_disconnect; for a failed CALL_ACCEPTED parse the earlier assignments (sk_state TCP_ESTABLISHED, state values) have already been made and are not undone.
note: Reviewer (malformed Clear Request skips disconnect) was right about the old wording; the earlier prose already described out_clear for it, rewritten to list each path explicitly. x25_in.c:97-155, out_clear at 150-155. Old prose said 'sk_state remains TCP_ESTABLISHED' for the short CLEAR_REQUEST case, which is not set by this function in that case.

name: x25_proc_init
prose: The file contains two definitions of x25_proc_init: this one, compiled when CONFIG_PROC_FS is defined, and a stub in the #else branch that does nothing and returns 0. The CONFIG_PROC_FS version (marked __init) calls proc_mkdir for 'x25' under init_net.proc_net; if that returns NULL it returns -ENOMEM immediately and removes nothing. It then calls proc_create_seq for 'x25/route', 'x25/socket' and 'x25/forward' (mode 0444); if any of the three returns NULL it calls remove_proc_subtree('x25', init_net.proc_net) and returns -ENOMEM. If all succeed it returns 0. The only values it returns are 0 and -ENOMEM.
note: x25_proc.c:165-189 (proc version) and 194-196 (#else stub returning 0). Round-15 reviewer right (the #else stub exists and returns 0); round-2 reviewer claim (no subtree removal after proc_mkdir failure) is consistent with the code and already in the prose.

name: xdp_umem_create
prose: Allocates a struct xdp_umem and registers a memory region for it. It does kzalloc(GFP_KERNEL); if that fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). It then calls ida_alloc(&umem_ida, GFP_KERNEL); if that returns a negative value it frees the umem and returns ERR_PTR of that value; otherwise the id is stored in umem->id. It then calls xdp_umem_reg(umem, mr); if that returns nonzero it calls ida_free on umem->id, frees the umem and returns ERR_PTR of the error. On success it returns the umem pointer, owned by the caller, with its id still allocated in umem_ida. On the three failure paths the umem allocation is freed and, once an id has been allocated, that id is released; anything xdp_umem_reg itself allocated or pinned is not released here.
note: Not a non-function: the slice holds the whole function xdp_umem_create (xdp_umem.c:250-274), only the old name was a placeholder. Fixed under the real name.

name: xfrm_nlmsg_put_compat
prose: Static helper that starts a compat (32-bit layout) netlink message for a native kernel-built message. The parameter type is an index into the message tables: the caller xfrm_xlate64 passes type = nlh_src->nlmsg_type - XFRM_MSG_BASE, and the function reads payload = compat_msg_min[type] and src_len = xfrm_msg_min[type] with no bounds check, and separately switches on nlh_src->nlmsg_type itself. If src_len < payload it warns once (WARN_ON_ONCE) and returns ERR_PTR(-EMSGSIZE) without touching skb. It calls nlmsg_put(skb, pid, seq, type, payload, flags) using the pid, seq, nlmsg_type and flags of nlh_src; if that returns NULL it returns ERR_PTR(-EMSGSIZE). Otherwise a header with payload bytes is now appended to skb and the payload is zeroed. It then fills the payload by nlmsg_type: for DELSA, DELPOLICY, FLUSHSA, FLUSHPOLICY, NEWAE, REPORT, MIGRATE, NEWSPDINFO, NEWSADINFO and MAPPING it warns if src_len != payload and copies src_len bytes; for NEWSA, NEWPOLICY, UPDSA and UPDPOLICY it warns if src_len != payload + 4 and copies payload bytes; EXPIRE, ACQUIRE, POLEXPIRE and ALLOCSPI are copied field by field with the compat layout; on success it returns the new header pointer. For GETSA, GETPOLICY, GETAE, GETSADINFO, GETSPDINFO and any other nlmsg_type it logs pr_warn_once and returns ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP) with the zeroed header left appended to skb.
note: Old prose precondition 'type equals nlh_src->nlmsg_type' was wrong: type is nlmsg_type - XFRM_MSG_BASE (xfrm_compat.c:309 and xfrm_xlate64 at ~303). Reviewer's round-1 claim (zeroed header still appended on EOPNOTSUPP) is right and kept; round-2 claim (type/nlmsg_type mismatch) is a caller obligation, now stated.

name: xfrm_input
prose: Receive path for an IPsec packet; it is also re-entered with encap_type -1 (asynchronous crypto resumption) or -2 (reconstructed inner packet). It does not require the caller to hold an explicit RCU read lock: the SA lookup xfrm_input_state_lookup asserts softirq context instead, and the function takes rcu_read_lock itself just before xfrm_rcv_cb and releases it on each path that took it. Return paths: (a) Drop (labels drop_unlock and drop, also reached when xfrm_rcv_cb(..., 0) returns nonzero after rcu_read_unlock): releases x->lock if held, drops the device reference if async is set, calls xfrm_rcv_cb(skb, family, xfrm_proto, -1), frees skb with kfree_skb and returns 0. An invalid-state drop with encap_type -1 drops the device reference before jumping. (b) Returns 0 without freeing skb when x->type->input or xfrm_inner_mode_input returns -EINPROGRESS (the device reference is dropped in these paths only if async is set). (c) After the SA loop, if the last SA is tunnel mode: clears secpath olen, drops a valid dst, drops the device reference if async, calls gro_cells_receive and returns 0. (d) Otherwise: err is -EAFNOSUPPORT if no afinfo exists for family, else the result of afinfo->transport_finish(skb, xfrm_gro || async); if the offload GRO flag xfrm_gro is set the secpath olen is cleared, a valid dst dropped and skb passed to gro_cells_receive whether or not err is zero; then the device reference is dropped if async, rcu_read_unlock is called and err is returned (skb is not freed here when afinfo is NULL and xfrm_gro is clear). While processing it updates SA statistics, replay state and lifetime counters under x->lock.
note: slice cut head and tail (function at xfrm_input.c:463-785). Reviewer claim (caller need not hold RCU) is partly right: no explicit RCU lock needed, but xfrm_input_state_lookup has lockdep_assert_in_softirq (xfrm_state.c:1216), and xfrm_state_lookup (which takes RCU itself) is not the function used here. Old prose wrongly said the GRO/transport path returns 0 and that the decap path is the only GRO hand-off.

Return paths: (a) Drop (labels drop_unlock and drop, also reached when xfrm_rcv_cb(..., 0) returns nonzero after rcu_read_unlock): releases x->lock if held, drops the device reference if async is set, calls xfrm_rcv_cb(skb, family, xfrm_proto, -1), frees skb with kfree_skb and returns 0. Reviewer round-15 (returns err after gro_cells_receive, not 0) right; round-2 (drop path returns without rcu_read_unlock) wrong: the drop label is only reached after rcu_read_unlock where RCU was taken (xfrm_input.c:~735 and ~750); old prose's 'RCU caller holds' also wrong.

name: xfrm_timer_handler
prose: hrtimer callback for an SA's mtimer; x is the xfrm_state containing it. It has a single return, reached after spin_unlock(&x->lock), so the lock taken at entry is released on every path. Under the lock it first calls xfrm_dev_state_update_stats. Then: if x->km.state is XFRM_STATE_DEAD it returns HRTIMER_NORESTART with nothing else done. If the state is XFRM_STATE_EXPIRED it takes the expired path. Otherwise, for a nonzero hard_add_expires_seconds whose time has passed: if XFRM_SOFT_EXPIRE is set in x->xflags it resets x->curlft.add_time and computes a new remaining timeout from saved_tmo and continues, else it takes the expired path; a hard_use_expires_seconds that has passed also takes the expired path. Remaining timeouts update next to the minimum. If x->km.dying is set it skips the soft checks and goes to the reschedule step; otherwise soft add and soft use lifetimes are evaluated (sets warn, clears XFRM_SOFT_EXPIRE or sets it with saved_tmo), x->km.dying is set to warn and km_state_expired(x, 0, 0) is called if warn. The reschedule step forwards the timer by next seconds and returns HRTIMER_RESTART if next != TIME64_MAX, else returns HRTIMER_NORESTART. The expired path sets an XFRM_STATE_ACQ state with zero SPI to XFRM_STATE_EXPIRED, calls __xfrm_state_delete, calls km_state_expired(x, 1, 0) only if that returned 0, audits with success flag err ? 0 : 1 and returns HRTIMER_NORESTART.
note: xfrm_state.c:642-735. Reviewer claims (DEAD path; hard add expiry with XFRM_SOFT_EXPIRE rescheduled) were already reflected in the earlier prose and are confirmed by the code.

name: verify_newsa_info
prose: Validates a new-SA netlink request: p is the xfrm_usersa_info, attrs the parsed attribute array, extack the error sink. It only reads its inputs (apart from setting extack messages) and returns 0 if every check passes, otherwise a negative errno, mostly -EINVAL with an extack message. In order it checks: p->family is AF_INET, or AF_INET6 (with CONFIG_IPV6, else -EAFNOSUPPORT); the selector family (p->family if the selector family is 0 and XFRM_STATE_AF_UNSPEC is clear) is AF_UNSPEC, AF_INET with prefix lengths <= 32, or AF_INET6 with prefix lengths <= 128 (or -EAFNOSUPPORT if IPv6 is disabled); the protocol is AH, ESP, COMP or (with IPv6) DSTOPTS/ROUTING, each with its own required and forbidden algorithm attributes, ESP TFCPAD only in tunnel mode, IP-TFS attributes only in IP-TFS mode, COMP SPI below 0x10000, DSTOPTS/ROUTING requiring XFRMA_COADDR; any other protocol is -EINVAL. It then returns the first nonzero result of verify_aead, verify_auth_trunc, verify_one_alg for AUTH, CRYPT and COMP, verify_sec_ctx_len and verify_replay. The mode must be transport, tunnel, route optimisation or BEET, or IP-TFS (only with ESP and with an in or out SA direction). Finally it checks XFRMA_MTIMER_THRESH (needs XFRMA_ENCAP, not on an output SA) and direction-specific flag and attribute restrictions for output SAs (DECAP_DSCP, ICMP, WILDRECV flags, replay_window, IP-TFS drop time and reorder window, nonzero replay seq/bitmap), input SAs (NOPMTUDISC flag, DONT_ENCAP_DSCP and OSEQ_MAY_WRAP extra flags, IP-TFS DONT_FRAG, INIT_DELAY, MAX_QSIZE and PKT_SIZE), and XFRMA_SA_PCPU without a direction, each returning -EINVAL.
note: Slice is the middle of verify_newsa_info (xfrm_user.c:251-580); name 'verify_xfrm_userstate' does not exist, function exists so FIXED not dropped (slice cut the head). The old dropped prose was too vague ('constraints hold').

name: aa_change_hat
prose: Changes to a hat (child profile) or, with count == 0, restores the saved label. hats is an array of count hat names (may be NULL when count == 0), token is the magic value stored or checked, flags may contain AA_CHANGE_TEST. It gets references on the current cred, the newest current label and the newest ctx->previous label and releases them before returning; the one reference it may keep is ctx->nnp, set to the current label if no_new_privs is set, the label is not unconfined and ctx->nnp is empty. Paths: if the current label is unconfined and none of its profiles in scope has children it audits and returns -EPERM. If count != 0 it calls change_hat: an error from it is returned unchanged with no further audit here (change_hat audits some failures itself); then a may_change_ptraced_domain error is audited and returned; then, if no_new_privs is set, the label is not unconfined and the new label is not an unconfined subset of ctx->nnp, it returns -EPERM without audit; then with AA_CHANGE_TEST it returns 0 without changing the label; otherwise it calls aa_set_current_hat(new, token): 0 on success (task label becomes the new hat label and token is stored), -EACCES is audited with kill permission (and kills the task) and returned, any other error is returned without audit. If count == 0, a previous label exists and AA_CHANGE_TEST is clear: with no_new_privs and a previous label that is not an unconfined subset of ctx->nnp it returns -EPERM without audit; otherwise aa_restore_previous_label(token) is called: 0 restores the label, -EACCES is audited with kill and returned, other errors are audited and returned. If count == 0 and there is no previous label or AA_CHANGE_TEST is set it returns 0 and changes nothing.
note: domain.c:1314-1426. Old prose overstated that all references are released (ctx->nnp keeps one) and that change_hat errors are always already audited (change_hat audits only when count > 1 or in complain mode, or on its own build errors). Reviewer claims (count==0 without previous returns 0; nnp -EPERM unaudited) confirmed. The restore-path nnp -EPERM check is also unaudited.

name: aa_change_profile
prose: Performs a one-way profile change for the current task. fqname is the target name (NULL or empty is rejected), optionally prefixed with '&' for stacking; flags may contain AA_CHANGE_ONEXEC, AA_CHANGE_STACK and AA_CHANGE_TEST. It first gets a cred reference and the current label, and may store a reference in ctx->nnp (no_new_privs set, label not unconfined, ctx->nnp empty). If fqname is NULL or empty it puts the label and returns -EINVAL without audit; on this path the cred reference taken at entry is not released by this function. Otherwise it parses fqname with aa_label_parse. If parsing fails: with AA_CHANGE_TEST or when the current profile is not in complain mode it audits and returns the audit result for that parse error; if in complain mode and AA_CHANGE_TEST is clear it creates a learning profile as the target (ENOMEM is audited and returned if that fails) and goes on to the ptrace check. If parsing succeeds it checks change_profile permissions for each profile in scope; a failure is audited inside the wrapper and returned. Then may_change_ptraced_domain is checked: an error is audited and returned unless every profile in scope is in complain mode, in which case the code continues. With AA_CHANGE_TEST it then returns the current error value (0 if none) without changing the label. For a non-stacking change it builds the new label; a build failure is audited as 'failed to build target label' with -ENOMEM or the build error; a no_new_privs violation returns -EPERM without audit. Without AA_CHANGE_ONEXEC it replaces the current label (merging with the target when stacking), with AA_CHANGE_ONEXEC it records the target as the on-exec label. Except for the early -EINVAL, the no_new_privs -EPERM, the permission-wrapper failure and the test-mode exit, the paths end at the audit step, and the returned value is the result of the audit calls for the (possibly zero) error.
note: domain.c:1479-1655. Reviewer claim (complain-mode learning profile continues) was already reflected; code confirms it (domain.c:~1532-1546). Old prose claim that all cred references are released is wrong for the -EINVAL early return (get_current_cred taken in declarations at ~1486, no put_cred before return at ~1507).

name: aa_alloc_root_ns
prose: Boot-time (__init) allocation of the AppArmor root namespace. It assigns the global root_ns from alloc_ns(NULL, 'root'); if that returns NULL it returns -ENOMEM. It then allocates the 'kernel_t' unconfined profile with alloc_unconfined; if that returns NULL it calls destroy_ns and aa_free_ns on root_ns and returns -ENOMEM, but the global root_ns is not reset to NULL on this path. On success it sets the global kernel_t to that profile's label, makes root_ns->unconfined->ns hold a reference to root_ns (aa_get_ns) and returns 0. It does not check that root_ns was previously unset.
note: policy_ns.c:365-384. Old prose said 'no root namespace remains allocated' after failure: the memory is freed but the global root_ns still points at it (no assignment to NULL). The old contract was dropped (touches globals; ensures clause omitted the real behaviour).

name: devcgroup_legacy_check_permission
prose: Checks whether the current task's device cgroup allows an access of the given type, major, minor and access mask. It holds rcu_read_lock across reading task_devcgroup(current) and across the exception matching, and releases it before returning. If the cgroup behaviour is DEVCG_DEFAULT_ALLOW it permits the access only when match_exception_partial finds no exception overlapping the request; otherwise (default deny) it permits only when match_exception finds an exception that fully covers the request. It returns 0 if permitted and -EPERM if not; it takes no reference and does not modify the cgroup. It dereferences the cgroup pointer without a NULL check.
note: device_cgroup.c:832-856. Old prose said the RCU lock is held only while reading the devcgroup; the code keeps it through the exception matching.

name: ima_collect_measurement
prose: Computes and stores the file digest in iint. If modsig is non-NULL, ima_collect_modsig is called first on every path. If IMA_COLLECTED is already set in iint->flags it then returns 0 without further work. Otherwise it calls vfs_getattr_nosec for STATX_CHANGE_COOKIE (i_version stays 0 if that failed or the mask lacks the cookie), initialises a zeroed hash buffer with the digest size of algo, and computes the digest: with IMA_VERITY_REQUIRED from ima_get_verity_digest (on failure result = -ENODATA, with audit cause no-verity-digest), else ima_calc_buffer_hash if buf is non-NULL, else ima_calc_file_hash. In the verity branch a successful lookup leaves result as returned by vfs_getattr_nosec. A nonzero result other than -EBADF or -EINVAL goes to the exit with that result. Otherwise it krealloc's iint->ima_hash (-ENOMEM on failure), copies the digest, stores i_version in iint->real_inode.version (when the real inode is the file inode) or through integrity_inode_attrs_store, and sets IMA_COLLECTED only if result is 0; with -EBADF or -EINVAL the digest and version are stored, IMA_COLLECTED stays clear and that errno is returned. At the exit, whenever result is nonzero, it takes a dentry name snapshot, emits an integrity audit message (cause failed(directio) if the file has O_DIRECT, else the cause set earlier) and releases the snapshot; the return value is result.
note: ima_api.c:~258-340 in the file (function named in slice head cut). Old prose precondition 'caller holds iint->mutex' removed because the function does not check it. Old prose omitted that in the verity branch an error from vfs_getattr_nosec survives.

name: is_ima_appraise_enabled
prose: Returns the result of ima_appraise & IMA_APPRAISE_ENFORCE converted to bool: true when bit 0x01 (IMA_APPRAISE_ENFORCE) of the global ima_appraise is set, false otherwise. It reads the global and has no side effects. The other IMA_APPRAISE_* bits (FIX 0x02, LOG 0x04, MODULES 0x08, FIRMWARE 0x10, POLICY 0x20, KEXEC 0x40) are ignored.
note: Reviewer right: ima.h:430 defines IMA_APPRAISE_ENFORCE as 0x01 and 0x08 is IMA_APPRAISE_MODULES; old contract tested the wrong bit. Contract left empty because the function reads global state.

name: process_measurement
prose: Applies the IMA policy to one file access and returns 0 or -EACCES; every other internal error is turned into one of those two. It returns 0 immediately, before taking any lock, if ima_policy_flag is clear or the inode is not a regular file, and also if ima_get_action returns no action and no read/write violation check is needed. Otherwise it records must_appraise = action & IMA_APPRAISE, takes the inode lock to get the iint (-ENOMEM becomes rc) and run ima_rdwr_violation_check, releases it, and for rc nonzero or no action jumps to the exit. With an action it takes iint->mutex, resets stale flags, and masks away work already done. If nothing remains to do, it still runs mmap_violation_check and ima_get_cache_status when must_appraise is set and may leave rc nonzero. Otherwise it reads xattr and modsig as needed and calls ima_collect_measurement; an error other than -EBADF and -EINVAL skips the rest. For READING_MODULE_COMPRESSED it clears must_appraise and stops. Otherwise it stores the measurement, runs ima_check_blacklist and ima_appraise_measurement (under the inode lock), mmap_violation_check, audit, clears rc if O_DIRECT is permitted, and rejects a digest algorithm not in allowed_algos with -EACCES. At out_locked rc becomes -EACCES for MAY_WRITE on an IMA_DIGSIG file that is not new; iint->mutex is released, xattr_value and modsig freed. At out the path buffer is freed; if must_appraise is nonzero and rc is nonzero and IMA_APPRAISE_ENFORCE is set it returns -EACCES; otherwise, if must_appraise is nonzero and the file is open for write, it sets IMA_UPDATE_XATTR in iint->atomic_flags (note: iint is NULL if ima_inode_get failed). In all remaining cases it returns 0. The function may update iint flags, measurement lists and audit records.
note: ima_main.c:~258-510. Round-15 reviewer right: the 'no remaining action' path (rc from mmap_violation_check) can yield -EACCES when must_appraise and enforce are set; the old prose said it yields 0. Also noted: if ima_inode_get fails (rc = -ENOMEM, iint NULL) with must_appraise set, not enforcing and FMODE_WRITE, the final set_bit uses &iint->atomic_flags with iint NULL. The caller-locks precondition was removed; function takes the inode lock itself.

name: ima_parse_rule
prose: Parses one IMA policy rule string into entry. It starts an audit record, sets uid/gid/fowner/fgroup to invalid values and the action to UNKNOWN, and splits rule in place on spaces and tabs with strsep (so rule is modified). Each token is matched against policy_tokens; parsing stops at the first token starting with '#' (treated as a comment, not an error) and at the next token after any earlier token set a negative result. Empty tokens are skipped. Per token it records the action (a second action sets -EINVAL), func, mask, fsmagic, fsuuid, uid/euid/gid/egid/fowner/fgroup with eq/gt/lt operators, LSM subject/object fields (via ima_lsm_rule_init), keyrings, label, digest_type, appraise_type, appraise_algos, pcr, template, permit_directio and appraise_flag, setting -EINVAL for malformed or repeated values of those fields and an unknown token, and passing on errno from kstrtoul, uuid_parse, ima_alloc_rule_opt_list or ima_lsm_rule_init (including -ENOMEM). fsname is the exception: a repeated fsname is not rejected; it overwrites entry->fsname with a new kstrdup (the old string is not freed here), and kstrdup failure gives -ENOMEM. After the loop, if result is 0 and ima_validate_rule fails the result is -EINVAL; if the action is APPRAISE and that condition is not taken (including when an earlier error made result nonzero) it ORs ima_appraise_flag(entry->func) into temp_ima_appraise. On success with modsig or verity rules it checks template descriptors (warnings only). It writes 'res=' to the audit record, ends it and returns result: 0, or a negative errno; entry may be partly filled on error.
note: ima_policy.c:1410-1677. Round-15 reviewer right: Opt_fsname has no duplicate check (ima_policy.c ~1521-1531). Additional finding: the 'else if (entry->action == APPRAISE) temp_ima_appraise |= ...' binds to the whole if, so it also runs after an earlier parse error. Old prose 'every duplicate token is -EINVAL' and 'audit in every case' were over-general.

name: ipe_parse_policy
prose: Parses p->text (textlen bytes) into a new struct ipe_parsed_policy stored in p->parsed. It returns -EBADMSG at once if p->textlen is 0; -ENOMEM if kmemdup_nul of the text fails; otherwise it allocates the parsed policy with new_parsed_policy (an error from it is returned). It then walks the duplicated text line by line (split on IPE_LINE_DELIM), removing comments and trailing spaces and skipping empty lines; the first non-empty line goes to parse_header and each later line to parse_rule, and a nonzero result from either is returned after freeing the partial parsed policy with ipe_free_parsed_policy. After the loop it returns -EBADMSG (freeing the parsed policy) if no header line was found or validate_policy returns nonzero. On success it stores the new parsed policy in p->parsed and returns 0; the caller must later free it with ipe_free_parsed_policy. On every path the duplicated text is freed, and p->parsed is not assigned on failure.
note: Real name is ipe_parse_policy (policy_parser.c:505). Old prose precondition 'parsed field not yet set' removed: the code never reads p->parsed.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE5(keyctl, u32, option, u32, arg2, u32, arg3, u32, arg4, u32, arg5)
prose: Generated function __do_compat_sys_keyctl(option, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5): the 32-bit compat keyctl entry point. It switches on option and returns directly the result of the matching handler, converting arguments that are user pointers with compat_ptr. It handles every command number 0 (KEYCTL_GET_KEYRING_ID) through 32 (KEYCTL_WATCH_KEY); for any other option value (for example option > 32) it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. For KEYCTL_PKEY_QUERY (24) it returns -EINVAL if arg3 is nonzero, otherwise it calls keyctl_pkey_query with arg2 and compat pointers for arg4 and arg5. The value returned is whatever the handler returns (0 or a positive value on success, negative errno on failure); this wrapper itself takes no locks or key references.
note: compat.c:17-132. The old contract was removed (the function calls out to handlers that touch global state, and the contract only covered two of many return paths). Name given as the macro head per rule 5.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(add_key, const char __user *, _type, const char __user *, _description, const void __user *, _payload, size_t, plen, key_serial_t, ringid)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_add_key: the add_key system call. _description may be NULL; a NULL or empty description lets the key type generate one. Steps and errors: -EINVAL if plen > 1048575 (1024*1024 - 1); the type string is copied with key_get_type_from_user (32-byte buffer): -EFAULT or another negative result from strncpy_from_user, -EINVAL if it is empty or has no NUL within 32 bytes, -EPERM if it starts with '.'. A non-NULL description is copied with strndup_user (limit 4096 bytes): -EFAULT if unreadable, -EINVAL if it does not fit in 4096 bytes including the NUL, -ENOMEM; an empty description is freed and treated as NULL; -EPERM if the description starts with '.' and the type begins with 'keyring'. If plen is nonzero the payload is copied into a kvmalloc buffer (-ENOMEM, -EFAULT). The keyring is looked up with lookup_user_key(ringid, KEY_LOOKUP_CREATE, KEY_NEED_WRITE) (its error is returned) and key_create_or_update is called; on success the new or updated key's positive serial number is returned, otherwise the negative error from key_create_or_update. On every path after allocation the description and payload are freed (payload with kvfree_sensitive) and the references on the keyring and returned key are dropped.
note: keyctl.c:~58-140. Reviewer round-1/2 claims (NULL description allowed; strndup_user gives -EINVAL not -E2BIG for overlong) are right and reflected; description limit is 4096 bytes including the NUL, so a 4096-character string is also rejected.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(request_key, const char __user *, _type, const char __user *, _description, const char __user *, _callout_info, key_serial_t, destringid)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_request_key: the request_key system call. Steps and errors: the type string is copied with key_get_type_from_user (-EFAULT or other negative result from the copy, -EINVAL if empty or without NUL in 32 bytes, -EPERM if it starts with '.'). The description is copied with strndup_user (limit 4096 bytes including NUL): -EFAULT, -EINVAL if too long, -ENOMEM. If _callout_info is non-NULL it is copied with strndup_user (limit PAGE_SIZE, same errors) and its length taken. If destringid is nonzero the destination keyring is looked up for writing (lookup_user_key error returned). The key type is looked up with key_type_lookup (its error, such as -ENOKEY for an unknown type, is returned). request_key_and_link then searches for the key and, if none is found and callout info was given, constructs one via the request-key upcall; its error is returned (for example -ENOKEY when nothing is found and no callout info was given). The result is then waited on with wait_for_key_construction(key, 1); a negative result (-ERESTARTSYS if interrupted, or a key state error) is returned; otherwise the key's positive serial number is returned. On every path the key reference, key type reference, destination keyring reference and the copied strings are released. The function's own comment says an empty callout string is changed to '-'; that conversion is not done in this function.
note: keyctl.c:~165-250. Reviewer claims: omitted -EINVAL for oversized description (true, now listed); empty callout_info changed to '-' (per the function comment, not performed here; stated as such). strndup_user returns -EINVAL, not -E2BIG (reviewer right, prose already says -EINVAL).

name: keyctl_reject_key
prose: Rejects (negatively instantiates) the key identified by id using the assumed authorisation key. error is unsigned and is validated first: it returns -EINVAL, with no other effect, if error is 0, is >= MAX_ERRNO (4095), or equals ERESTARTSYS (512), ERESTARTNOINTR (513), ERESTARTNOHAND (514) or ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK (516). Then: -EPERM if the current cred has no assumed request_key_auth key; -EKEYREVOKED if request_key_auth_get returns NULL for it; -EPERM if the target key's serial differs from id (reference on rka released); the negative result of get_instantiation_keyring if the destination keyring selected by ringid cannot be obtained; otherwise the result of key_reject_and_link(target, timeout, error, dest_keyring, instkey). The destination keyring reference is dropped after that call and the request_key_auth reference is dropped on every path after it was obtained. Only if key_reject_and_link returns 0 is the assumed authority cleared with keyctl_change_reqkey_auth(NULL); on any failure it stays assumed.
note: keyctl.c:~1295-1355. Reviewer round-2 (MAX_ERRNO is 4095, error 4095 is rejected) right; old text already used 4095. Removed the unverified wording on writability of the destination keyring; the code only shows a negative return from get_instantiation_keyring.

name: tpm2_seal_trusted
prose: Seals payload->key into a TPM2 key blob. It returns -EINVAL before touching the TPM if options->hash is not in tpm2_hash_map or options->keyhandle is 0. It then calls tpm_try_get_ops (returning its error directly) and tpm2_start_auth_session; from here every return goes through tpm_put_ops. If the session start fails that error is returned and payload->blob_len is not modified. tpm_buf_init and tpm_buf_init_sized failures end the auth session and return the error (payload->blob_len not modified). After both buffers exist, a failure of tpm_buf_append_name or tpm_buf_fill_hmac_session, of the transmit/HMAC response check, an overflow of the command buffer (-E2BIG, with tpm2_end_auth_session called here), a blob length above MAX_BLOB_SIZE or a boundary error (-E2BIG), or a truncated response blob (-EFAULT) jumps to the common exit, which destroys both buffers, maps a positive TPM return code to -EINVAL for TPM2_RC_HASH and -EPERM for any other, and, whenever blob_len is not negative, stores blob_len into payload->blob_len (0 if the length was never read; the unvalidated length from the TPM on the -E2BIG and -EFAULT blob paths). On the success path blob_len is the result of tpm2_key_encode; if that is negative it becomes the return value. The function calls tpm2_end_auth_session itself only on the buffer-init and overflow paths shown; whether the session is ended on the other failure paths is decided inside the callees and is not visible in this function.
note: Real name tpm2_seal_trusted (trusted_tpm2.c:241); tpm2_seal_cmd does not exist, slice cut the head, so FIXED not dropped. Old prose missed that payload->blob_len is overwritten on the failure paths that reach the common exit, including with an unvalidated length.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(landlock_restrict_self, const int, ruleset_fd, const __u32, flags)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_landlock_restrict_self: the landlock_restrict_self system call. It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if Landlock is not initialised, -EPERM if the task has neither no_new_privs nor CAP_SYS_ADMIN in its user namespace, and -EINVAL if flags has bits outside LANDLOCK_MASK_RESTRICT_SELF. Unless ruleset_fd is -1 and flags is exactly LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF, it takes the ruleset from the fd with get_ruleset_from_fd(fd, FMODE_CAN_READ) and returns that error if it fails. It then calls prepare_creds (returning -ENOMEM on failure) and, with CONFIG_AUDIT, updates the log_subdomains_off flag in the new credentials. If there is no ruleset (the fd -1 case) it returns the result of commit_creds(new_cred). Otherwise it merges the new credentials' domain with the ruleset using landlock_merge_ruleset; on an error it calls abort_creds and returns that error. On success it (with CONFIG_AUDIT) sets the logging fields, releases the old domain reference, installs the merged domain in the new credentials and returns commit_creds(new_cred). The reference to the ruleset taken from the fd is released automatically on every return.
note: syscalls.c:~477-543. Old prose precondition was wrong as a precondition (invalid inputs are handled by error returns) and the postcondition omitted -EOPNOTSUPP, -EPERM and -EINVAL. Name given as the macro head per rule 5.

name: selinux_netcache_avc_callback
prose: AVC callback taking an event code; its only return statement returns 0. If event equals AVC_CALLBACK_RESET it calls sel_netif_flush, sel_netnode_flush and sel_netport_flush, then synchronize_net(), which blocks until a network RCU grace period has elapsed. For any other event value it does nothing and returns 0.
note: Reviewer's earlier ordering concern checked: flush calls come before synchronize_net (hooks.c, function body). Prose unchanged in substance.

name: selinux_lsm_notifier_avc_callback
prose: AVC callback taking an event code; its only return statement returns 0. If event equals AVC_CALLBACK_RESET it calls sel_ib_pkey_flush() and then call_blocking_lsm_notifier(LSM_POLICY_CHANGE, NULL), which runs the registered blocking LSM notifiers and may sleep. For any other event value it does nothing and returns 0.
note: Code matches earlier prose; reviewer's contract complaints no longer apply (no contract).

name: selinux_msg_queue_msgsnd
prose: Checks whether the current task may send msg to the queue msq. It reads the current SID at entry and the queue and message security structures. If the message's SID is SECINITSID_UNLABELED it calls security_transition_sid(current sid, queue sid, SECCLASS_MSG, NULL, &msec->sid) to label it; if that returns nonzero it returns that error at once without any permission check. Then it calls avc_has_perm in order: current SID needs MSGQ__WRITE on the queue SID; if that returned 0, current SID needs MSG__SEND on the message SID; if that returned 0, the message SID needs MSGQ__ENQUEUE on the queue SID. It returns the result of the first avc_has_perm call that returned nonzero, or 0 if all returned 0 (avc_has_perm can return 0 in permissive mode despite a denial). msqflg is not used.
note: hooks.c body matches the earlier prose; only added the permissive-mode caveat on the avc_has_perm result.

name: smack_inode_removexattr
prose: Checks and applies removal of an xattr on a dentry's backing inode. If name is one of XATTR_NAME_SMACK, XATTR_NAME_SMACKIPIN, XATTR_NAME_SMACKIPOUT, XATTR_NAME_SMACKEXEC, XATTR_NAME_SMACKTRANSMUTE or XATTR_NAME_SMACKMMAP and the caller does not pass smack_privileged(CAP_MAC_ADMIN) it returns -EPERM with no further effect. For every name (Smack or not) it then performs smk_curacc on the inode's label for MAY_WRITE, passes the result through smk_bu_inode, and returns that result if nonzero with no state change. If the check passed it updates Smack state only for four names: XATTR_NAME_SMACK on a non-socket inode sets smk_inode to the superblock default label; XATTR_NAME_SMACKEXEC sets smk_task to NULL; XATTR_NAME_SMACKMMAP sets smk_mmap to NULL; XATTR_NAME_SMACKTRANSMUTE clears SMK_INODE_TRANSMUTE in smk_flags. XATTR_NAME_SMACK on a socket, SMACKIPIN, SMACKIPOUT and any non-Smack name change nothing. It then returns 0. idmap is unused.
note: smack_lsm.c function body checked; old prose correct, reworded for clarity (non-Smack names still go through the MAY_WRITE check, as the round-2 reviewer said).

name: tomoyo_condition
prose: Evaluates the parsed condition cond against request r (cond may be NULL; the caller is documented as holding tomoyo_read_lock). Returns true at once if cond is NULL. Returns false at once if argc or envc in cond is nonzero and r->ee is NULL or r->ee->bprm is NULL. Otherwise it walks the condc elements; argv and envp elements are skipped for now. A name-union element (right operand a name union) compares the symlink target (needs obj and its symlink_target) or runs tomoyo_scan_exec_realpath; a mismatch gives false; any other left operand with a name union is skipped. Numeric or bit-operation elements take their values from the current task ids and pid/ppid, file type and mode constants, bprm argc/envc (false if bprm is NULL), number unions (range or group comparison) or object stat fields; stat fields need obj (false if NULL) and call tomoyo_get_attributes once to set obj->validate_done, and false results if the stat entry is invalid or the operand index is unknown. A bit operation is accepted only when the other operand is one of the PATH*_PERM operands (two bit-op operands give false); other comparisons test range overlap against the element's equals flag. The first element that fails returns false. After all elements, if r->ee is non-NULL and argc or envc is nonzero it returns tomoyo_scan_bprm(...) for the argv and envp elements; otherwise true. The function takes no locks itself, and its only side effect is possibly filling obj->stat and obj->validate_done.
note: Function is tomoyo_condition (condition.c:765-1122); this slice is its tail. Old prose said false when argc/envc nonzero 'while r->ee is NULL' but the code also gives false when r->ee is non-NULL with a NULL bprm; fixed. Unmatched left operand with a name union is silently skipped (switch with only two cases).

name: tomoyo_get_condition
prose: Parses the condition part of a TOMOYO rule from param->data, a string of space-separated $left$op$right blocks where op is '=' or '!=' (left must not contain '=' or ' '). It first calls tomoyo_get_transit_preference, which may consume a leading transit-domain or path/keyword token into a name reference held in a local entry template; if that fails the string is replaced by '/' so parsing fails. It runs two passes: a dry run that counts elements and validates the syntax, overwriting separators with NUL, and, after restoring the separators, a second run that fills the newly kzalloc'd entry (sized from the counts, GFP_NOFS). The separators are restored between the passes only; they are not restored before the function returns, on success or on failure. A block without '=' or with '==' or an empty left side, a bad argv/envp/number/name union, or a bad or repeated grant_log value fails parsing. On success it returns the result of tomoyo_commit_condition for the new entry: either the new entry added to tomoyo_condition_list or an existing identical entry with its user count incremented (the new one is freed), or NULL if the policy lock wait is interrupted or the memory quota is exceeded. The returned entry owns the transit name reference. On any parse error or kzalloc failure it frees any partially built entry, drops the transit name reference and returns NULL.
note: condition.c:495-757. Old prose wrongly claimed the separator characters are restored before every return: after the second pass and on every goto out the string is left with NULs (the restore loop at condition.c ~734-748 only runs before 'goto rerun'). Also removed the claim that the caller holds tomoyo_read_lock (not stated for this function).

name: tomoyo_condition
prose: Evaluates the parsed condition cond against request r (cond may be NULL; the caller is documented as holding tomoyo_read_lock). Returns true at once if cond is NULL. Returns false at once if argc or envc in cond is nonzero and r->ee is NULL or r->ee->bprm is NULL. Otherwise it walks the condc elements; argv and envp elements are skipped for now. A name-union element (right operand a name union) compares the symlink target (needs obj and its symlink_target) or runs tomoyo_scan_exec_realpath; a mismatch gives false; any other left operand with a name union is skipped. Numeric or bit-operation elements take their values from the current task ids and pid/ppid, file type and mode constants, bprm argc/envc (false if bprm is NULL), number unions (range or group comparison) or object stat fields; stat fields need obj (false if NULL) and call tomoyo_get_attributes once to set obj->validate_done, and false results if the stat entry is invalid or the operand index is unknown. A bit operation is accepted only when the other operand is one of the PATH*_PERM operands (two bit-op operands give false); other comparisons test range overlap against the element's equals flag. The first element that fails returns false. After all elements, if r->ee is non-NULL and argc or envc is nonzero it returns tomoyo_scan_bprm(...) for the argv and envp elements; otherwise true. The function takes no locks itself, and its only side effect is possibly filling obj->stat and obj->validate_done.
note: No function tomoyo_evaluate_cond exists; this slice (782-1064) is the middle of tomoyo_condition (condition.c:765-1122), so fixed under the real name, same prose as the 1065-1122 entry. Old contract named element_matches, which does not exist, and its prose said 'iff every element matches' ignoring the argv/envp scan and several unconditional false returns.

name: aesni_cipher_mac
prose: Computes the authentication digest for crp using the session's hash functions (ses->hash_init, hash_update, hash_finalize), inside fpu_kern_enter and fpu_kern_leave. The key is crp->crp_auth_key if non-NULL, else csp->csp_auth_key, of length csp->csp_auth_klen. If ses->hmac is set it computes HMAC: inner hash over (key XOR 0x36 padded to SHA1_BLOCK_LEN) then the AAD (from crp->crp_aad or via crypto_apply), then the payload (from the output buffer if there is one and the operation is encrypt, else the input), then 4 bytes of crp_esn if CSP_F_ESN is set; then an outer hash over (key XOR 0x5c padded) and the inner digest, and the key pad buffer is zeroed. This function does not check that keylen fits SHA1_BLOCK_LEN. Without HMAC it hashes AAD and payload directly. After leaving FPU mode, if CRYPTO_OP_VERIFY_DIGEST is set it copies ses->mlen bytes of the digest from the request and returns EBADMSG if timingsafe_bcmp reports a difference; otherwise it writes ses->mlen digest bytes into the request at crp_digest_start. It returns 0 except for EBADMSG. The local digest buffer res is zeroed only on the paths that do not return EBADMSG; on EBADMSG res and res2 are not zeroed, and the hash context sctx is never zeroed.
note: slice (790-868) is the tail of aesni_cipher_mac (aesni.c:771-868); 'hmac_hash_process' does not exist. Old drop prose said scratch buffers are zeroed; they are not on the EBADMSG path.

name: intel_sha256_step
prose: Runs the SHA-256 compression function over num_blks consecutive 64-byte blocks starting at data, using Intel SHA extensions. It loads the eight 32-bit state words from digest (digest[0..7], unaligned load), reorders them, and for each block (while num_blks > 0) performs the 64 rounds and adds the result to the saved state, advancing data by 64 bytes. Afterwards it reorders the state back and stores the eight words into digest with aligned 128-bit stores, so digest must be 16-byte aligned. Only complete blocks are processed; no padding is done. With num_blks == 0 the state is only re-ordered and stored back unchanged. It touches no global state.
note: Real function intel_sha256_step (intel_sha256.c:65); 'sha256_block_transform' does not exist, slice is the tail. Old prose said digest holds 'initial' state; it is the current state of any partially hashed message.

name: armv8_crypto_cipher_process
prose: Runs the session's cipher over crp's payload. If the algorithm is CRYPTO_AES_NIST_GCM_16 it uses crp->crp_aad as the AAD buffer when non-NULL, otherwise it obtains one with armv8_crypto_cipher_alloc (contiguous subsegment or a malloc copy); if no buffer can be obtained it returns ENOMEM before any other work, so the iv and tag buffers are not zeroed on that path. It then sets up buffer cursors, re-keys the session with armv8_crypto_cipher_setup if crp->crp_cipher_key is non-NULL (the return value is ignored), reads the IV and enters FPU mode. For CRYPTO_AES_CBC it returns EINVAL (after the common cleanup) if the payload length is not a multiple of AES_BLOCK_LEN, else encrypts or decrypts; XTS and GCM encrypt or decrypt; GCM encrypt writes the tag to crp_digest_start and GCM decrypt reads the tag and sets error to the result of armv8_aes_decrypt_gcm (nonzero when verification fails). Any other cipher algorithm leaves the payload untransformed and returns 0. After fpu_kern_leave it frees the AAD buffer only if it was allocated here, zeroes the local iv and tag with explicit_bzero, and returns error (0, EINVAL or the GCM decrypt error). This function does not wipe the session key schedules; the caller keeps ownership of ses and crp.
note: armv8_crypto.c:~302-377. Reviewer round-2 (ENOMEM path skips zeroing iv/tag) right and stated; round-1 claim that old prose said keys are wiped is addressed. Note: armv8_crypto_cipher_alloc allocates crp_payload_length bytes but copies aad length bytes (armv8_crypto.c ~283-290), outside this function.

name: blake2_cipher_process
prose: Computes a BLAKE2 MAC over crp's payload and verifies or stores it. The key is crp->crp_auth_key if non-NULL, else csp->csp_auth_key, with length csp->csp_auth_klen; output length is ses->mlen. Inside fpu_kern_enter and fpu_kern_leave (always paired) it selects on csp->csp_auth_alg: for CRYPTO_BLAKE2B or CRYPTO_BLAKE2S it initialises the state (the keyed init when klen > 0), failing with EINVAL if the init returns nonzero; applies the payload with crypto_apply and, if that returns nonzero, remembers that error; and calls the final function into a local buffer, failing with EINVAL if it returns nonzero. Any other algorithm hits __assert_unreachable. If an error was recorded it returns it (the crypto_apply error or EINVAL). Otherwise, with CRYPTO_OP_VERIFY_DIGEST it copies ses->mlen bytes from crp_digest_start and returns EBADMSG if timingsafe_bcmp differs, else 0; without it, it copies the digest to crp_digest_start and returns 0. The local digest buffers and hash state are not zeroed.
note: Real function blake2_cipher_process (blake2_cryptodev.c:251); slice is its tail. Old prose said errors returned 'EINVAL if init or final fails' correctly; added that nothing is zeroed and that crypto_apply error is propagated only after the FPU leave.

name: ccp_queue_get_ring_space
prose: Static inline helper returning the number of free slots in the queue's ring as an unsigned value: (1 << sc->ring_size_order) - ccp_queue_get_active(qp) - 1, where sc is qp->cq_softc and ccp_queue_get_active returns (qp->cq_tail - qp->cq_head) masked with (1 << ring_size_order) - 1. One slot is always left unused. It reads qp and the softc and modifies nothing.
note: ccp.h:248-256: slice is just the return statement of ccp_queue_get_ring_space. Old contract removed because the function reads fields through pointers.

name: md5block
prose: Static function, compiled only when MD5_ASM is not defined. It loads ctx->state[0..3], then for each complete 64-byte block (while len >= MD5_BLOCK_LENGTH) reads the block as sixteen little-endian 32-bit words with le32dec, runs the 64 MD5 steps in four rounds of 16, adds the result to the running state, and advances p and len by MD5_BLOCK_LENGTH. After the loop it stores the four state words back into ctx->state. Any trailing len % 64 bytes are ignored; with len < 64 the state is stored back unchanged. The data pointer need not be aligned.
note: Real function md5block (md5c.c:~147-318); 'MD5Transform' is not defined in this file's slice, the slice is the tail of md5block.

name: rijndaelDecrypt
prose: Decrypts one 16-byte block: reads ct[0..15] as four big-endian words, XORs the first round key rk[0..3], applies Nr - 1 table-driven inverse rounds with the Td0..Td3 tables and the following round keys (the unrolled build performs rounds 1-9 and extra rounds only when Nr > 10 and Nr > 12; the loop build iterates Nr >> 1 times with two rounds per iteration), then applies the final round with the Td4 table and the last round key and writes the 16 plaintext bytes to pt[0..15]. rk must hold the decryption key schedule of 4*(Nr+1) words. It has no return value and modifies only pt.
note: slice is the tail of rijndaelDecrypt (rijndael-alg-fst.c:1032-1221); 'AES_decrypt_tail' does not exist. Old prose treated this as a fragment.

name: cd9660_vget_internal
prose: Finds or creates the vnode for inode number ino. Returns: (1) vfs_hash_get error, or an existing vnode found (in *vpp), returned as is (0 if found). (2) A failure of getnewvnode returns the error with *vpp set to NULLVP. Otherwise it allocates a zeroed iso_node, links it to the vnode, takes the vnode lock and calls insmntque: on error it frees the iso_node, sets *vpp to NULLVP and returns the error. (3) vfs_hash_insert error, or another thread's vnode returned in *vpp, is returned as is. (4) If isodir is NULL it reads the directory record from the device: ESTALE (after vput) if the block number is beyond volume_space_size, if the record would cross a logical block, or after the read if the record length would cross the block (also releasing the buffer); a bread error is returned after vput. If relocated is set it reads the first block of the directory with cd9660_blkatoff and uses its '.' entry (vput and error return if that fails). It then sets iso_extent, i_size and iso_start from the record, sets timestamps and attributes (via cd9660_defattr/cd9660_deftstamp for plain ISO 9660, or cd9660_rrip_analyze for RRIP), releases the buffer, sets the vnode type from the inode mode (using cd9660_fifoops for FIFOs, otherwise VN_LOCK_ASHARE), sets VV_ROOT if iso_extent equals root_extent, marks the vnode VSTATE_CONSTRUCTED with vn_set_state, stores it in *vpp and returns 0. Note that brelse(bp) after the attribute switch is unconditional while bp is NULL when isodir was supplied and relocated is 0.
note: slice (779-850) is the tail of cd9660_vget_internal (cd9660_vfsops.c:671-850). Prose written from the full function. The last sentence reports an observed code path (cd9660_root passes a non-NULL isodir with relocated 0 for non-RRIP media); I did not verify what brelse does with NULL.

name: devfs_open
prose: VOP_OPEN for devfs. ap->a_vp is expected locked on entry; if the driver is called the function unlocks it first and relocks it with vn_lock(vp, vlocked | LK_RETRY) before returning on every path after the unlock. Returns: ENXIO if vp->v_type is VBLK or v_rdev is NULL (nothing else touched). Otherwise if dev->si_iosize_max is 0 it is set to DFLTPHYS. Then dev_refthread: if it returns NULL (no reference was taken) it returns ENXIO; if a_fp is NULL and the driver has d_fdopen it releases the reference with dev_relthread and returns ENXIO. Otherwise, for VCHR it adds a usecount, unlocks the vnode, sets td_fpop to fp, and if fp is non-NULL sets fp->f_data and fp->f_vnode; then calls d_fdopen if present else d_open(dev, a_mode, S_IFCHR, td). On a nonzero result it clears any cdevpriv. td_fpop is restored, the vnode is relocked, on error with VCHR the usecount is subtracted, and dev_relthread releases the reference. On error it returns the driver's error with ERESTART turned into EINTR; fp->f_data and f_vnode stay set. On success with fp NULL it returns 0; with fp non-NULL and f_ops == badfileops it calls finit(fp, fp->f_flag, DTYPE_VNODE, dev, &devfs_ops_f); then returns 0.
note: devfs_vnops.c:1281-1349. Reviewer right: when dev_refthread returns NULL no reference exists, so nothing is released (old prose claimed a release). Everything else in the old prose checked against code and kept, with the NULL-fp/d_fdopen path correct.
